title: Reuse before you recycle
description: A jar, a shirt, a box: most things can live a second life before they become recycling.

body.heading: Second-life thinking
paragraphs: Before binning anything, ask: Could this hold something, become something, or serve someone else? Glass jars become storage, old t-shirts become cleaning cloths, and sturdy boxes become organisers.
Repair is reuse too. A sewn button, a glued handle, or a replaced phone battery can add years to an item at a fraction of the cost and footprint of a new one.

body.heading: Pass it on
paragraphs: Things you no longer need may be exactly what someone else is looking for. Donate, swap, sell, or give away usable items through local groups, charity shops, or school exchanges.
Keeping items in use is one of the simplest environmental wins: no new manufacture, no disposal, and someone else saves money too.

body.heading: Buy with a second life in mind
paragraphs: When you do buy, favour things that are repairable, refillable, or useful in more than one way. Their second life is decided on the day you choose them.

takeaway: Ask of everything: can it be reused, repaired, or passed on before it is recycled?
